title: The subject and the wanted admission

captions.physics: Speaking of a possible calmer continuation
captions.energy: Returning to the objection’s actual subject
captions.emotions: Feeling attached to a wanted admission

meaning: You can speak of a possible calmer continuation and return to an objection’s actual subject, noticing attachment to an admission without which an answer feels insufficient.
text: The Star in the physical position of your Vishuddha appears in speaking of a possible calmer continuation. The Chariot in energy supports a wish to return to the objection’s actual subject and understand the answer’s substance. The Devil in emotions brings attachment to a wanted admission: particular words may feel like a condition for satisfaction with the exchange. You can hope for clarity while noticing that explanation alone seems insufficient. This experience does not prescribe the answer another person owes.

For example, after a sharp comment comes the hope, “We can discuss this calmly later”. Returning to the subject, you establish what the criticism concerned. **A clear conversational subject does not guarantee a wanted admission**. Even a substantial explanation may bring little relief if “You are right” is strongly wanted. You can name which part makes sense and which confirmation you desire. The conversation’s direction stays distinguishable without presenting hunger for one phrase as the sole purpose assigned to both.

Difficulty grows if every new argument is assessed only as progress towards that admission. Conversation seems unfinished regardless of substance already heard. The constructive Chariot helps retain the actual question and distinguish it from an emotionally wanted ending. You can miss the expected words and still understand the comment more accurately; open hope for continuation promises neither compulsory victory nor the disappearance of all frustration after the first substantial answer.
